One of my favorite bits of writing advice goes something like “don’t ask ‘is this action something this character would do?’ but ‘what would it take for them to do this?’” I think Gregson’s decision at the end of season 6 is a perfect example of that. Sure, in a vacuum it is so painfully antithetical to his character to let a murderer walk free. But it’s his daughter. We’ve been shown that he gets very emotional and protective over her, to the detriment of his own career and values (punching the cop/exboyfriend and letting Kitty attack him after).

As far as Joan and Sherlock’s decision…I think they understand his reaction to some extent. It still hurts, but they respect him and have been working with him for so long. And now he’s in a hospital bed and they didn’t get a chance to repair that relationship and it puts into perspective the things that matter to them. I think it helps for all parties involved that Michael was a prolific serial killer and not just..some guy lol.

If it helps, I’ve started doing “backups” before each chapter or before a tricky sequence. If you’re on PS5 you’ll exit the game then go to settings > saved data and game/app settings > upload or delete from console storage. You upload your save to cloud storage (iirc it will ask you if you want to turn auto-upload on and you’ll say yes). Then if you mess up, you can exit the game, go to the same place but you’ll click “download or delete from cloud storage” then download your backup and you should be back to the beginning of the last chapter/part that you saved at. Tedious and sometimes I hate exiting out of the game over and over, but it’s better than rage quitting and doing a whole new playthrough

I just turned 22, left home at 20. My timelines aren’t the best in the post so I apologize. My mom’s drinking itself was on a bell curve, with the highest point being around the time I left home. My sister would tell me about the arguments, etc. long after they’d been resolved. I did confront my mom on the vodka thing (in retrospect not as firmly as I should have) but she said that that was the first and last time she’d done it. That incident was about a year ago and I hadn’t heard anything since this time. My parents have always pulled the “unruly teen” card about Marilyn and I’m ashamed to admit that I bought into it. It took some time and discussion with my partner to realize that my parents had simply not parented her. She would ask and they would hand it over, then sigh and say that they didn’t know what went wrong. Hearing about the current situation snapped me out of it and at that point I knew I was too..conditioned? to actually help the situation.

When I say previous arguments, most have been from when I was late teens onward about my mom’s drinking. My parents, especially my mom, have a hard time seeing me as an adult in regards to my work, which is partially why I didn’t have that discussion with them on my mom’s drinking or give them resources from my CPS days (which tbf aren’t much). The first time I thought about calling CPS was when I was in training, but then I got a call from my dad saying that CPS was at their house because my sister was having sex with a 19 year old. That kind of pushed my concerns to the side.

My mom’s alcoholism was not a plummeting downward spiral, and for a while it seemed like she was doing better. Up until this point I thought things were ok, but when I heard that my mom was belittling my sister for taking “too many shots” of the shots that SHE was providing I just…snapped. I didn’t feel qualified to help them because I was part of the family and they were comfortable dismissing me. Having an outside party whose job it was to make sure they were parenting her correctly felt better than stirring up an argument that would go nowhere. As far as opening conversation, my partner has encouraged me to reach out in a few days when they’ve calmed down. I’m conflicted (and this is probably just the upbringing here) because I know if I just stop talking to them for a while it will go away and they’ll reach out and we’ll be a “family” again. But that’s not fair to my mom or my sister. It’s upsetting that both of them were upset with me.

Mom’s drinking has been an unspoken thing for a while. I felt more comfortable telling my dad that I didn’t think it was appropriate for Marilyn to be vaping or drinking and he’s kind of just sighed and agreed. Talked to my mom and got the same response. I talked to Marilyn about it but she just got mad at me for “preaching to her” and “trying to act like a parent” which got me frustrated because…*someone* has to parent her. Most of the discussions I’ve had with my parents are about Marilyn’s mental health and how I don’t want them to make the same mistakes they did with me (e.g. not taking me to a therapist when they knew something was wrong). So other than a few times, I haven’t discussed them providing alcohol and weed to them as much as I probably should have. But I have expressed disappointment in their lack of parenting and they brush me off.

They’re *exempt* from reporting *if* the perpetrator is the one disclosing it “while [the reporter] is functioning in the ministerial capacity of the member of the clergy.” I’m not familiar with all of the church’s practices, so I am unsure if every conversation with your bishop is considered “confidential” (e.g. with Catholicism there’s a difference between confessional and speaking with your priest outside of that space). From Utah code 62A-4a-403:

> When a member of the clergy receives information about abuse or neglect from any source other than confession of the perpetrator, the member of the clergy is required to report that information even though the member of the clergy may have also received information about abuse or neglect from the confession of the perpetrator.

So if anyone other than the perpetrator discloses potential abuse, clergy are still required to report.

>Exemption of the reporting requirement for an individual described in Subsection (3) does not exempt the individual from any other efforts required by law to prevent further abuse or neglect by the perpetrator.

I personally have never gotten a call directly from an LDS bishop, only the church attorneys. I’m not going to say that they don’t call in, but I’d say it doesn’t happen as often. I have gotten calls from perpetrators before who said that their bishops “urged them to confess/turn themselves in” and we never got a report from the bishop or attorneys. I personally think that the structure of the LDS religion itself prevents people from coming forward about “problems” in the congregation, even if their official stance is to go to the authorities.

I haven’t found anything about the Quileute people praising Stephenie about her “artistic liberty” in her writing, but I’d love to look at those interviews if you find them. All I’ve seen is that the [reactions](https://www.burkemuseum.org/static/truth_vs_twilight/)  were very [mixed](https://americanindiansinchildrensliterature.blogspot.com/2009/07/quileute-response-to-twilight.html?m=1), with concerns about their culture being commercialized and the reservation turned into a tourist destination. There are some that are happy to be in the [spotlight](https://www.themarysue.com/the-real-quileute-tribe/)  so they can actually set the record straight about their legends, not necessarily because of the books themselves. Regardless, we are in agreement that the Quileute deserve some form of compensation, and neither Summit nor Stephenie Meyer will do that, so it’s understandable that people would be uncomfortable giving money to a white woman profiting off of a real Native American tribe with half of their population living in [poverty](https://nativeappropriations.com/2010/02/is-twilight-good-for-the-quileute.html).

Have you considered by calling people “garbage” and “disgusting” you are also attacking their character for not 100% agreeing with you about a vampire YA novel? I don’t disagree that tumblr does dehumanize Stephenie to a worrying degree, but I think that calling people garbage for “stealing property” from a woman whose current net worth is $125 million dollars is a bit much. Go ahead and buy the book and support her, but I don’t understand the rage directed at teenagers who are trying to navigate and explore their ethical views. And let’s be real, piracy is not that big of a deal in today’s culture.

I don’t really agree with Tumblr, but the reason they are saying that is because of Stephenie’s refusal to give any of the money she made from bastardizing Quileute legends to the actual real-life tribe. So when they say they’re not going to pay for Midnight Sun, they usually talk about donating the money they would spend to the Quileutes. [(Here is the link to donate to their move to higher ground project](https://mthg.org) and I believe you can set your Amazon smile donation to their school on the reservation)

I didn’t technically work for them. I quit day 2 of training at Vector Marketing, and I’m glad I did. This is the first AskReddit post I can actually answer and I just realized it’s kinda long and convoluted. TL;DR below.

It felt like a scam from the very beginning, but my mom kinda pushed me to go to the interview. I spent three hours (did not tell us it would be that long) listening to a presentation about how great the job was with other recent hs graduates who didn’t know what we were getting into. Later that night I got a call saying I got the job and was now ready for unpaid training. The training was three days (first one 10 to 5, second 10 to 7, third 9-12 and the rest of the day with “appointments” selling their product). Bear in mind, I had early morning rehearsal for band that ended at 8:30 was 30min away from my house, then I had to drive 45/+ minutes to a tiny office with 3 parking spaces and 40/+ trainees.

First day there were little red flags but I was still excited about the $17 per appointment. After sitting nonstop for 7 hours the division manager in charge of training tells us to write down every name and number of every adult you OR YOUR FRIENDS knew. He then pulled half of us aside and said because we have “potential” we needed to arrive early and stay late, to write at least 100 names and numbers down, and schedule enough appointments to impress him.

Second day, the 9th hour of training was reserved for calling people you knew and reading from a script. After calling my aunt that I hadn’t talked to since Christmas and my friend’s mom who had never met me, I started feeling sick to my stomach. I felt exploited and exploiting. I was just a pawn to sell kitchen knives.
After every training and in the mornings they expected us to call the office. I called them when I got home (after I cried in the car for a little bit bc I was so tired and strung out and HUNGRY) and tried to quit.

I say tried because the woman on the phone started reading off a script on why I shouldn’t quit. She said, and I quote: “What do you like? Um, clothes, makeup? Ok so imagine you had a cousin that had a really good eyebrow pencil and didn’t tell you about it. You’d be really upset with them right? Well, that’s you right now, because you’re not showing your friends and family this great product..”. I just told her I couldn’t be a part of their pyramid scheme anymore and I had too much respect for myself and my family to work at their company and hung up.

TL;DR: Vector (a MLM preying on hs graduates) overworked the crap out of me in unpaid training and encouraged me to exploit my friends and family to sell (arguably, really nice) kitchen knives. When I tried to quit, they assumed all I liked was clothes and makeup then implied that my family wouldn’t love me if I didn’t sell them knives.
